html:
The Duchy of Nassau was a small German state on the right bank of the Rhine, north of Mainz, that existed from 1806 to 1866. Its capital became Wiesbaden, a spa town.

It was formed when two branches of the House of Nassau merged their lands and joined Napoleon's Confederation of the Rhine. After 1815 it was a member of the German Confederation. In 1814 it was one of the first German states to get a written constitution.

In the Austro-Prussian War of 1866 Nassau backed Austria. Prussia won and annexed it. The deposed duke, Adolphe, later inherited the throne of Luxembourg in 1890, through the family link with the Dutch House of Orange-Nassau, and his descendants still reign there.
